nodes.summary: The cells `H[i+1][j+1], H[i+1][j+2], …` of a row from the remaining letters `b :: ys` of the second sequence, the remaining cells `up :: prev` of the previous row, the previous row's cell `diag` to the upper left and the cell `left` just computed. A previous row that is too short ends the row early (this does not happen for rows of the table, `nextRow_eq`).
nodes.title: Auxiliary row computation for the Smith–Waterman table

nodes.summary: From the row of the prefix `px`, `nextRow` computes the row of `px ++ [a]`: the cells `H[i+1][j] = swCellScore σ gap (px ++ [a]) py` for the prefixes `py` of `ys`, shortest first.
nodes.title: One row of the table

nodes.summary: The row of the table for the prefix extended by `a`, from the previous row: `H[i+1][0] = 0`, then the recurrence left to right.
nodes.title: Next row of the Smith–Waterman table

nodes.summary: The Smith–Waterman table, filled row by row over the remaining letters of the first sequence: `row` is the current row and `best` the largest cell of the earlier rows.
nodes.title: Row-by-row filling of the Smith–Waterman table

nodes.summary: The table computes the optimal local alignment score (Smith–Waterman 1981, `gap ≤ 0`): `swTab` is the maximum, over all pairs of infixes of `xs` and `ys` (including the empty ones, which give the floor `0`), of their optimal global alignment score `nwScore`.
nodes.title: The table computes the optimal local alignment score

nodes.summary: `swTab` is the largest cell `swCellScore σ gap px py` over all pairs of prefixes.
nodes.title: The table computes the Smith–Waterman score

nodes.summary: The largest cell of the `(|xs| + 1) × (|ys| + 1)` table, with the zero row `H[0][j] = 0` to start.
nodes.title: The Smith–Waterman table

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
